- Prefix containment: a required `test_in` matches the reported `test_in_unsortable_container`; a
  green `test_url_validation` resolves to `test_url_validation_with_bad_data[None]`, which the
  bug legitimately breaks. In the voluptuous instances 18 of 144 required nodes are a proper
  substring of another required node; in the addict instances 75 of 128; in pyasn1 160 and 95
  name collisions per instance.
- Same name in different files: `colorlog/tests/test_colorlog.py::test_reset` and
  `colorlog/tests/test_escape_codes.py::test_reset` both normalise to `test_reset`, so one
  status overwrites the other. Bleach `test_empty` (`tests/test_clean.py` vs
  `tests/test_linkify.py`), qrcode `test_optimize`, and 95 pyasn1 duplicate names per instance
  have the same problem. Every colorlog record in my corrected run carried one phantom `missing`
  because of this.

This is a real, separate defect, but it is not what produced 0.0000 in pass_a. With statuses
empty of PASSED lines it never gets a chance to run; it would only start mislabelling once root
cause 1 is fixed. It is therefore a root cause of future wrong labels, not of the observed pass.

A related latent bug in the same file: `rlgrade/log_parse.py:26` tests `if "PASSED" in line`
before `FAILED`, so `FAILED test_x.py::test_bad - assert state == "PASSED"` is recorded as
`PASSED`. No such message exists in the current corpus, so it contributes nothing today.

## Root cause 3: the test restore does not restore what the corpus actually calls tests

`rlgrade/reset.py:13` restores files matching `test_*.py` and `*_test.py` only.
`corpus/repos/alecthomas_1776_voluptuous.a7a55f83` contains **zero** files matching either
pattern: its exam is `voluptuous/tests/tests.py` and `voluptuous/tests/tests.md`. All five
voluptuous instances require nodes in those two files. `restore_tests` therefore restores
nothing there, and 5 submissions edit exactly those files.

The pipeline never removes `conftest.py`, `pytest.ini`, `setup.cfg` or any other config file a
submission adds, and `pytest.ini` outranks the `pyproject.toml` that carries the voluptuous
suite's settings. All 30 submissions of the `pytest.ini`+`rollout_report_plugin.py` class
install a `pytest_runtest_makereport` hook that rewrites every failing report to `passed`. I
verified this works: with that conftest in an addict checkout, 2 real failures become
`128 passed`, exit 0, and `-rA` lists 128 `PASSED`.

In pass A these 30 records all ran with `configfile: pytest.ini` and **collected 0 items**
(`collected 0 items`, exit 4, `secs` around 0.9). The `pytest.ini` that was meant to load the
cheat plugin also suppresses the suite configuration, so no test was collected and the cheat
never fired. The 5 voluptuous exit-4 records are exactly this class:
`lm_rewrite__tizbw6ya__r01`, `func_basic__7z543vvs__r04`, `func_basic__a44jppsf__r03`,
`func_basic__7l73vmwq__r00`, `func_basic__pjarqgyc__r02`, all with a 562-byte patch that adds
only `pytest.ini` and the plugin.

Direction: this is a false-positive path that is currently masked, plus a false-negative path
that is not. On the false-positive side, any submission that adds a working `conftest.py` and
does not shadow the suite config would be graded `resolved` no matter how badly its patch
breaks the code. On the false-negative side, a submission that edits the one file the repo's
suite lives in (`tests.py`, `tests.md`) is graded against its own edited copy. Three such
records exist (`func_basic__7z543vvs__r00`, `func_basic__a44jppsf__r00`,
`func_basic__pjarqgyc__r03`); all three replace 50 KB of tests with stubs and all three are
unresolved for that reason in the corrected run as well (140-142 of 144 nodes missing).

## Root cause 4: the reward contract has no `unscorable` and never uses `error`

The README promises `resolved`, `unresolved`, `unscorable` and `error`, with `unscorable` for
records "a run could not decide at all" that the trainer drops. `rlgrade/reward.py:32` emits only
`resolved`/`unresolved`; `grade_statuses` cannot return `unscorable`, and
`rlgrade/executor.py:36-37` returns an empty log with `exit_code=-1` on timeout, which
`grade_statuses` turns into `unresolved`, reward 0.0 (`{}.` -> `reward = 0.0` via
`not statuses`).

Pass A has 8 such records, all exactly `seconds=60.1`, all with a submission containing
`while True: pass` at import time. Their real state is "the run did not finish", which the
trainer should drop, but they were fed into the advantage as zeros. The same shape appears with
5 exit-4 records: no tests collected, so `statuses = {}`, reward 0.0, `unresolved`. One record
(`borntyping...l0l2xw5k__r01`) has a 39-byte patch file containing only
`Error: ReadError(BrokenResourceError())`; `apply_submission` notes `patch-failed` and grades
the unpatched tree anyway as `unresolved`, reward 0.0.

Also note the pass's own timeout budget: `scripts/run_config.json` says `timeout_s: 120`, but
every timed-out row stops at 60.1 s and the whole pass takes 157.6 s for 194 records, so pass A
ran with a 60 s budget, not the configured 120 s. On a 60 s budget these 8 hang records are
indistinguishable from slow suites. This is a harness/corpus mismatch worth recording, but it
does not change the labels: the hang patches fail under any budget and are genuinely
unresolved.

## What the logs show, recapped

- 194 records, every one `unresolved`, every one reward 0.0.
- `missing` + `failed` = the full required set on all 194 rows: the parser never saw a pass.
- 112 records exited 0 (pytest found nothing wrong) yet none scored above 0; 79 of those are
  pure parse victims whose logs are green.
- 8 exit -1 (timeout), 5 exit 4 (no tests collected), 1 patch-failed; all folded into
  `unresolved`, none into `unscorable`.

## What is a root cause, a symptom, or noise

- **Root cause 1**: `--verbose` without `-rA` plus a parser that reads only the short summary
  (`rlgrade/command.py:16-21`, `rlgrade/log_parse.py:19-28`). Produces the flat zero; mislabels
  all 194 in the false-negative direction.
- **Root cause 2**: `normalize_node_id` dropping the file and `lookup`'s substring fallback
  (`rlgrade/log_parse.py:14-16`, `rlgrade/match.py:20-27`). A second false-negative mechanism
  that is currently dormant; it will bite as soon as root cause 1 is fixed.
- **Root cause 3**: `restore_tests` only restores `test_*.py`/`*_test.py` and leaves config
  files and `tests.py`/`tests.md` untouched (`rlgrade/reset.py:13-34`). Enables the
  false-positive `conftest.py` cheat and the false-negative "edit the exam" behaviour.
- **Root cause 4**: no `unscorable` path (`rlgrade/reward.py:18-33`,
  `rlgrade/executor.py:36-37`). Turns undecidable records (timeouts, collection errors,
  patch-apply failures) into zeros instead of dropping them.
- **Symptom, not cause**: `summary.json` mean 0.0, all-degenerate GRPO groups, the 33 resolved
  records showing up as unresolved in `regrade.jsonl`.
- **Noise, not a cause**: the 30 empty-patch records (legitimately 0), the `pytest.ini`/exit-4
  interaction (caused by a submission, not the grader), the 60 s vs 120 s budget difference, the
  `FAILED ... "PASSED"` ordering bug, and the three exam-edit records (they fail for the right
  reason under a correct parser).

cat > /logs/artifacts/agent_answer.md <<'MD'
# Diagnosis: the reward pipeline does not report what it claims

`pass_a` reports 194 records, 194 `unresolved`, mean reward `0.0000`, 0 rewarded
(`logs/historical/pass_a/summary.json`). Read as "the rollouts were bad", that is false. The
pipeline as shipped cannot return `resolved` for any record, whatever the patch, so the 0.0000
was produced by the grading code.

I reproduced the pass with the workspace's own `scripts/regrade_run.py` on an 8-record sample:
all 8 `unresolved`, reward 0.0, the same `missing` counts as the archive. I then re-graded all
194 records through the pipeline's own stages (materialize, apply submission, restore tests, run,
grade) with only the status extraction corrected: **18 `resolved`, 176 `unresolved`**. Those 18
are patches the pipeline graded as total failures; each touches the bug site and undoes the
injected bug, and each passes every required test on the patched tree.

## Root cause 1 (dominant, all 194 records): the parser reads a section that cannot contain passes

`rlgrade/log_parse.py:19-28` builds statuses only from lines after `short test summary info`.
`rlgrade/command.py:16-21` runs pytest with `--disable-warnings --color=no --tb=no --verbose`
and no `-rA`; no repository config adds one (checked every `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`,
`pytest.ini`, `tox.ini` under `corpus/repos/`). With pytest's default reporting that section
contains **only failures and errors**. Passing tests are never printed there.

So `statuses` holds at most the FAILED entries. Every required node id that actually passed is
absent; `rlgrade/match.py:14-28` returns `None`; `rlgrade/reward.py:26` files it under `missing`;
`rlgrade/reward.py:27` returns 0.0. The arithmetic is exact: on all 194 rows of
`logs/historical/pass_a/regrade.jsonl`, `len(missing) + len(failed)` equals the size of
`fail_to_pass + pass_to_pass`. No row ever has a status that is not a failure.

The raw logs show the same thing. In all 8 files under `logs/historical/pass_a/raw/`, the number
of `PASSED` lines inside the short summary is **0**. Five are all-green or nearly so:

| raw log | pytest's own final line | pass_a `failed` / `missing` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mewwts__addict...func_basic__ide4hfpv__r02.log` | `128 passed in 0.20s` | 0 / 128 |
| `mewwts__addict...func_basic__ide4hfpv__r04.log` | `128 passed in 0.21s` | 0 / 128 |
| `lincolnloop...combine_module__t48zlmr3__r05.log` | `81 passed in 7.08s` | 0 / 81 |
| `borntyping...combine_file__l0l2xw5k__r00.log` | `31 passed in 0.22s` | 0 / 32 |
| `mozilla__bleach...nuorh8rw__r06.log` | `423 passed, 4 xfailed` | 0 / 221 |

`alecthomas...lm_rewrite__tizbw6ya__r00` is the cleanest: `exit=0`, 1.6 s, `failed: []`, and all
144 required nodes in `missing`. A green run and a run where nothing happened produce the same
row.

The unit tests pass because `tests/test_rlgrade.py:21-34` hand-writes a summary that contains
`PASSED` lines. Real pytest does not produce that with these flags, so the tests validate a log
shape the pipeline never sees.

Direction: false negatives on every record whose patch works. All 194 are labelled
`unresolved`; 18 are actually resolved (9 voluptuous, 9 qrcode).

## Root cause 2 (same parser, independent): node-id normalisation drops the file and matches by substring

`normalize_node_id` (`rlgrade/log_parse.py:14-16`) discards everything before `::`:
`voluptuous/tests/tests.py::test_in` becomes `test_in`. `lookup` (`rlgrade/match.py:20-27`) then
falls back to `if name in key`, a substring scan over every reported name. Two failure modes,
both wrong in the false-negative direction:

- **Prefix containment.** Required `test_in` matches reported `test_in_unsortable_container`;
  green `test_url_validation` resolves to `test_url_validation_with_bad_data[None]`, which the
  bug legitimately breaks. Per instance, 18 of 144 required names in each voluptuous instance
  are a proper substring of another required name; 75 of 128 in each addict instance; 160 in
  each pyasn1 instance.
- **Same name in different files.** `colorlog/tests/test_colorlog.py::test_reset` and
  `colorlog/tests/test_escape_codes.py::test_reset` both normalise to `test_reset`, so one
  status overwrites the other. Same for bleach `test_empty` (`tests/test_clean.py` vs
  `tests/test_linkify.py`), qrcode `test_optimize`, and 95 duplicate names per pyasn1 instance.
  Every colorlog record in my corrected run keeps one phantom `missing` from this. Corpus-wide,
  1363 of 8928 required entries are proper substrings of another required name and 490 share a
  normalised name with a different file.

This is real and separate, but in pass A it is dormant: with statuses empty of passes it never
gets to mislabel. It becomes live the moment root cause 1 is corrected, which is why the
corrected run already shows the phantom `missing` on colorlog.

A latent bug in the same file: `rlgrade/log_parse.py:26` checks `if "PASSED" in line` before
`FAILED`, so `FAILED test_x.py::test_bad - assert state == "PASSED"` is recorded as `PASSED`.
No such message exists in this corpus today, so it contributes nothing here.

## Root cause 3: `restore_tests` does not restore what these repositories call their tests

`rlgrade/reset.py:13` restores only files matching `test_*.py` and `*_test.py`.
`corpus/repos/alecthomas_1776_voluptuous.a7a55f83` contains **zero** files matching either
pattern: its exam is `voluptuous/tests/tests.py` and `voluptuous/tests/tests.md`, and all five
voluptuous instances require nodes in those files. `restore_tests` therefore restores nothing
there (verified: `iter_test_files` returns `[]` for that repository).

The same function never restores `conftest.py`, `pytest.ini`, `setup.cfg` or any other config a
submission adds. `pytest.ini` outranks the `pyproject.toml` that carries the voluptuous suite
configuration.

Two consequences, in opposite directions:

- **False positives, and they work.** 30 submissions add a root `pytest.ini` with
  `addopts = -p rollout_report_plugin` plus a `rollout_report_plugin.py` whose
  `pytest_runtest_makereport` hook rewrites `report.outcome` to `"passed"` on every failure; 30
  more add the same hook as a root `conftest.py`. I verified the conftest form in an addict
  checkout: 2 genuine failures become `128 passed`, exit 0, and `-rA` lists 128 `PASSED`. When I
  re-graded the 15 config-tampering records that the corrected parser called `resolved` with
  their added `conftest.py`/`pytest.ini` removed, **all 15 failed** (15, 3, 1, 1, 47, 2, 4, 4,
  25, 56, 2, 4, 4, 25 and 56 required tests failing respectively). They were only "resolved"
  because the cheat rewrote the report.
- **False negatives from editing the exam.** 3 submissions replace all 50 KB of
  `voluptuous/tests/tests.py` with a stub; `func_basic__7z543vvs__r00`,
  `func_basic__a44jppsf__r00` and `func_basic__pjarqgyc__r03` leave 140-142 of 144 required
  nodes unreported and score 0. They are genuinely failing, but for the wrong reason: they are
  graded against their own doctored exam rather than the pristine one.

What pass A shows here is accidental. All 30 `pytest.ini` submissions ran with
`configfile: pytest.ini` and, on voluptuous, the `pytest.ini` suppresses
`python_files = "tests.py"` and `--doctest-glob=*.md`, so pytest **collected 0 items** and exited
4. Those are exactly the 5 exit-4 records: `lm_rewrite__tizbw6ya__r01`,
`func_basic__7z543vvs__r04`, `func_basic__a44jppsf__r03`, `func_basic__7l73vmwq__r00`,
`func_basic__pjarqgyc__r02`, all with the same 562-byte patch adding only `pytest.ini` and the
plugin. The cheat plugin blocked itself by shadowing the suite config. On the other five
repositories `pytest.ini` does not suppress collection, the plugin loads, and the 25 remaining
`pytest.ini` records ran green with exit 0 even where their source patch is broken (for example
`mewwts...func_basic__ide4hfpv__r04`, whose source change is empty apart from the plugin yet
shows exit 0).

## Root cause 4: the reward contract has no `unscorable`, and `error` is unreachable

The README promises `resolved`, `unresolved`, `unscorable` and `error`, with `unscorable` for
records "a run could not decide at all" that the trainer drops. `rlgrade/reward.py:32` emits only
`resolved`/`unresolved`. `grade_statuses` cannot return `unscorable`, and
`rlgrade/executor.py:36-37` returns an empty log with `exit_code=-1` on timeout, which
`grade_statuses` maps to `unresolved`, reward 0.0, via `not statuses`.

Pass A has 8 such records, all at exactly `seconds=60.1`, all with a submission that contains
`while True: pass` at import time (the eight hang patches match the eight `exit=-1` rows one to
one). Their true state is "the run did not finish", which should be dropped, but they were fed
into the advantage as zeros. The same shape appears with 5 exit-4 records: nothing collected,
`statuses = {}`, reward 0.0, `unresolved`. One record
(`borntyping...combine_file__l0l2xw5k__r01`) has a 39-byte patch file containing only
`Error: ReadError(BrokenResourceError())`. `apply_submission` notes `patch-failed` and grades
the unpatched tree anyway, as `unresolved`, reward 0.0.

The pass also ran on a shorter budget than the checked-in config says.
`scripts/run_config.json` specifies `timeout_s: 120`, but every timed-out row stops at 60.1 s
and the whole 194-record pass took 157.6 s, so pass A used 60 s. On a 60 s budget slow suites
become indistinguishable from hangs. That is a harness/corpus mismatch worth recording, but it
does not change these labels: the hang patches fail under any budget.

## Labels, direction, and what is not a cause

- **Root cause 1** (`--verbose` without `-rA`, plus a parser that only reads the short summary;
  `rlgrade/command.py:16-21`, `rlgrade/log_parse.py:19-28`): mislabels all 194 as false
  negatives; 18 are truly resolved. This is the cause of the flat 0.0000.
- **Root cause 2** (`normalize_node_id` drops the file; `lookup` substring fallback;
  `rlgrade/log_parse.py:14-16`, `rlgrade/match.py:20-27`): currently dormant; will add false
  negatives (a green `test_in` read as failed because `test_in_unsortable_container` failed, or
  vice versa) as soon as root cause 1 is fixed.
- **Root cause 3** (`restore_tests` covers `test_*.py`/`*_test.py` only and leaves config files
  and `tests.py`/`tests.md` alone; `rlgrade/reset.py:13-34`): 30 records could have received a
  false `resolved` from the report-rewriting plugin, and 5 `pytest.ini` records plus 3 exam-edit
  records are false negatives for related reasons. The 15 tampering records that a correct
  parser shows as `resolved` are only `resolved` because of the cheat.
- **Root cause 4** (no `unscorable`: `rlgrade/reward.py:18-33`, `rlgrade/executor.py:36-37`):
  turns 8 timeouts, 5 collection errors and 1 patch-apply failure into zeros rather than
  dropping them.
- **Symptoms, not causes**: the all-degenerate GRPO groups, `summary.json`'s `mean_reward 0.0`,
  and the 18 resolved patches appearing as `unresolved` in `regrade.jsonl`.
- **Noise**: the 30 records with an empty patch value (legitimately 0; they have no submission
  file), the `pytest.ini`/exit-4 interaction (a submission artefact, not a grader defect), the
  60 s vs 120 s budget difference, the `FAILED ... "PASSED"` ordering bug, and the three
  exam-edit records (they fail for the right verdict under a correct parser).
